text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, the late bloomer's breakout after years of working up from the ECHL. In his first full season in Seattle, the goals have gone quiet: three in 18 games, none in his last ten, and two points over that stretch.

Our read is that this one is a real dip, not just bad luck. His own chances over those ten games are down, 1.9 expected goals (the quality of chances) against 2.5 usually, and Seattle takes only 41% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, more than 4 points worse than without him. For the season, his three goals on 4.3 expected aren't far off. The problem isn't finishing. It's that the looks aren't coming the way they did.

The profile hasn't changed. He's a big, fast shooter whose offense lives in transition, with 53% of his shots off the rush by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and our model compares him to Owen Tippett. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 97th-percentile competition last season. Our talent range still has him around 25 goals. Watch the rush chances: when Seattle starts creating them again, he will too.
